caption: Did David’s everlasting house predict Jesus? The New Testament deliberately presents him as David’s lasting heir, though a dynastic promise cannot identify him alone.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did David’s house point to Jesus? God promises that David’s family and throne will endure. The New Testament presents Jesus as David’s lasting heir.
slides.body: God promises that David’s family and throne will endure. The New Testament presents Jesus as David’s lasting heir.
slides.heading: Did David’s house point to Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of 2Sam 7:16: Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me.
slides.body: Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me.
slides.heading: 2Sam 7:16

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Rev 22:16, BSB: “I, Jesus, have sent My angel to give you this testimony for the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star.”
slides.body: “I, Jesus, have sent My angel to give you this testimony for the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star.”
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Rev 22:16

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The Davidic claim is deliberate Luke places Jesus in David’s family. Revelation calls him both David’s root and his descendant.
slides.body: Luke places Jesus in David’s family. Revelation calls him both David’s root and his descendant.
slides.heading: The Davidic claim is deliberate

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But a dynasty includes many people The verse promises David an enduring royal house. It does not describe one unique future descendant.
slides.body: The verse promises David an enduring royal house. It does not describe one unique future descendant.
slides.heading: But a dynasty includes many people

title: David's house forever
